advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether nested `_call_with_keepalive` (memo-over-steering) double-instrumentation of a single tool call is acceptable, or emit at only one wrapper layer.
evidence: agent_call.py:196 `return await _call_with_keepalive(name, self._call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool))`
agent_call.py:314 `toolsets = _steering_toolsets(...)` then agent_call.py:321 `toolsets = _memo_toolsets(tools, toolsets, ...)` — memo wraps steering, so both fire on one call
Global coalescing in keepalive.py:29 suppresses the inner emits within 25s, so effect is redundancy/`call` index skew, not lost or spurious output
advisory.finding: When tool-step steering is active, toolsets nest (`_memo_toolsets` wraps `_steering_toolsets` per agent_call.py:314/321), so a single tool call passes through `_call_with_keepalive` twice — once in `_MemoNudgeToolset.call_tool` and again in the wrapped `_SteeringToolset.call_tool` — producing redundant nested start/complete emit attempts and double-incrementing the shared `_call_index` for one logical call.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives a workflow step through the interpreter and asserts both `workflow-step-start` and `workflow-step-complete` keepalive lines are emitted with op=<step id>.
evidence: search_files for `workflow-step-start` / `workflow-step-complete` returns ONLY the interpreter.py source lines — no test references either phase.

tests/unit/test_llm_keepalive.py has no test in which the dispatched/wrapped call raises — `_WrappedToolset` and `_SlowWrappedToolset` both `return "ok"`; `_call_with_keepalive`'s finally-on-exception path is likewise never exercised.
advisory.finding: The new workflow-step keepalive emissions in interpreter.py (workflow-step-start at line 509 and workflow-step-complete at line 514) have no test. These are newly added (+) lines; a regression that dropped either emission — or reordered them relative to step_identity — would not be caught. The keepalive test module covers the runner llm-call-start and tool-call phases but never drives a workflow step.
merged_from: The workflow-step-complete keepalive is emitted from a `finally` block (interpreter.py:513-514) so that completion is signalled even when `_dispatch` raises, but no test exercises that failure path. The completion-on-error cleanup contract is untested: a change that moved the emit out of `finally` into the try body would still pass every existing test yet silence the completion keepalive whenever a step raises.

runner.py:587-588 comment: "a slow/serial fan-out (e.g. the container per-child loop) is visible"
The single global window means N concurrent branches collectively emit at most one keepalive per 25s, not one per branch
dropped.finding: Keepalive coalescing state (`_last_emit_at`, `_call_index`) is process-global module state shared across all concurrent LLM/tool/workflow operations. Under the documented fan-out (container per-child loop), concurrent operations share a single 25s suppression window, so progress from one parallel branch suppresses keepalives for the others, weakening the multi-call progress visibility the feature exists to provide.
